transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?
Well, my wife thinks I’m not eating enough. Most days I’ll have coffee and toast in the morning, and maybe soup or some vegetables later on. Big meals just seem unnecessary at my age.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss over the past few months?

My doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. I suppose I have lost some weight, but I don’t really see it as a problem—being lighter makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up on my walks.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any change in your mood, or in your interest or enjoyment of activities you used to like doing?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed much change. I still do the things I usually do, more or less.
When mealtime comes, do you actually feel hungry, or do you find you get full very quickly or just don't feel like eating?
I usually don’t feel I need much. Coffee and toast in the morning is enough, and later I might have some soup or vegetables. Big meals just seem unnecessary at my age.
Have you or your family noticed any recent problems with your memory, such as forgetting appointments, misplacing things, or repeating questions?
I haven’t noticed any problems like that myself. I might forget a small thing now and then, but nothing that seems unusual to me.
Have you noticed any stomach pain, bloating, diarrhea, or changes in your bowel movements, such as blood in your stool?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that. Nothing that’s stood out to me.
Have you noticed any night sweats, fevers, or unusual tiredness over the past few weeks?
No, I can’t say I’ve noticed any of those things recently.
Have you noticed any new lumps, swelling, or enlarged glands anywhere on your body, such as in your neck, armpits, or groin?
No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or swelling anywhere.
Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer in the past, or has anyone in your immediate family had cancer?
I’m not really sure about my family history, doctor. I haven’t been diagnosed with anything like that myself.
Do you ever have trouble swallowing food, or does swallowing cause you any pain or discomfort?
No, I haven’t had any trouble swallowing, and it hasn’t been painful.
When it's time to eat, do you actually feel a lack of desire or appetite for food, or do you still feel hungry but just choose to eat smaller amounts?

I don’t really feel much need for a big meal. I’ll have coffee and toast in the morning, and maybe some soup or vegetables later. My wife says it isn’t enough, but big meals just seem unnecessary at my age.
Do you feel that your reduced eating is because you simply don't feel hungry, or do you eat about the same as before yet still keep losing weight?
I just don’t feel like I need much food. Coffee and toast in the morning is usually enough, then maybe soup or some vegetables later. Big meals feel unnecessary to me.
How long has this pattern of eating very little and not feeling hungry been going on—has it been like this for years, or did it start more recently?

It’s been this way for a while, really. I just don’t see the need for big meals—coffee and toast in the morning, then some soup or vegetables later is usually plenty for me. My wife is the one who feels it isn’t enough.
Has your weight stayed about the same over the past few weeks, or do you feel it's continuing to drop?
I think it has been dropping some. My doctor says the number is too low, but honestly, being lighter makes it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up on my walks.
If you made an effort to eat more at meals, do you think your weight would stabilize, or do you feel it might keep dropping regardless of how much you eat?

I suppose if I really made myself eat more, it might help. But most days I just don’t feel I need more than coffee and toast, then maybe soup or vegetables later. Big meals seem unnecessary at my age.
When it's near mealtime, do you ever notice physical signs of hunger—like your stomach growling or feeling empty—even if you don't feel like eating much?

Not really. I mean, I might have coffee and toast in the morning, then later some soup or vegetables, and that seems like enough to me. My wife thinks I’m not eating enough, but big meals just feel unnecessary at my age.
When you sit down to eat, do you find you have little desire to start eating at all, or do you begin eating normally but then feel full very quickly after just a few bites?

I don’t really feel much desire for a big meal to begin with. Coffee and toast in the morning is usually enough, and later I might have some soup or vegetables. My wife says it isn’t enough, but big meals just seem unnecessary at my age.
Do you know approximately how many pounds or kilograms you've lost over the past few months?
I’m not sure of the exact number. My doctor says the scale has gotten too low, but I feel lighter makes it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.

You mentioned your eating pattern has been like this for a long time—did your weight loss also start a long time ago, or did the weight loss only begin more recently, even though your eating habits stayed the same?

I’m not sure when it started exactly. My doctor says my weight has gotten too low, but I don’t really see it as a problem—I feel lighter on my feet, and it helps me get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Was your weight actually stable for years while you were eating this way, and has it only started dropping noticeably in the past few months?
I can’t really say when it changed. My doctor says the number on the scale is too low now, but I feel like being lighter helps me get around the garden and keep up with my walks.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a chronic, longstanding pattern of markedly reduced food intake and diminished desire/hunger for meals, which he rationalizes as normal for his age. This has resulted in associated unintentional weight loss noted by his physician and wife. Extensive review of systems (mood, GI symptoms, swallowing difficulty, malignancy signs, cognitive decline, systemic symptoms) was negative, ruling out depression, GI pathology, malignancy, or dementia as causes. Since the core presenting symptom is a primary lack of appetite/hunger (anorexia) rather than an isolated finding of weight loss without appetite change, R63.0 (Anorexia) is the most fitting principal diagnosis, with the associated weight loss (R63.4) captured as a related manifestation.
